messages:
sara-support: Heads-up — Skyline (tenant skyline-prod-72) is hitting widespread 429s and long tail latency on Dedicated since ~02:10 UTC. Customer says some requests time out. We see repeated kvcache evictions and autoscaler denials in our logs.

mike-eng-runtime: Can you paste sample logs + the exact tenant id (thanks). Also list whether these are long-context requests or short ones. @jin-ml to help analyze KV growth.

sara-support: tenant=skyline-prod-72. Sample logs:
```
[02:12:03] kvcache: evict key=ctx_72_abc size=1.3MB slab=27 -> free=0.2MB
[02:12:03] serve: 429 tenant=skyline-prod-72 reason=kvcache_throttle
[02:12:45] autoscaler: scale_down blocked by slab_pressure tenant=skyline-prod-72
```
Customer says most payloads include ~25k tokens (conversation + doc context). They also received a billing overage alert for burst usage.

jin-ml: 25k tokens per request will blow past our typical KV working set assumptions. Expect both slab fragmentation and big entries that are expensive to evict. Question: are they pinned to a shared Dedicated pool or have shard isolation? @elaine-sre do we have tenant slab metrics?

elaine-sre: Quick snip from metrics around 02:10 UTC: 
```
slab: total=64GB used=61GB fragmented=8GB
kvcache: entries=1.2M avg_size=2.1k tail>64k=4300
alloc: skyline-prod-72 = 18GB, growth_rate=600MB/min
autoscale: 02:11 request scale_up 2 gpus -> DENIED capacity_policy=reserved_burst_exhausted
```
So autoscaler requests were denied due to reserved/burst exhaustion on the fleet. That leaves us unable to add capacity quickly.

ops-bot: [AUTO] 02:12:15 autoscaler: request tenant=skyline-prod-72 add=2 nodes -> DENIED reason=reserved_burst_exhausted

mike-eng-runtime: Denied scale + exploding kvcache explains the 429s. Immediate mitigations to try: (1) reduce tenant max_sequence_tokens to cap KV footprint, (2) enable aggressive prefix/KV pruning for repeated doc chunks, (3) temporarily lower concurrency for that tenant. Can support push a config override?

sara-support: I asked Skyline to accept a temporary limit. They'll try 8k tokens max for 30 minutes. Applying override now:
```
POST /internal/tenants/skyline-prod-72/config
{ "max_sequence_tokens": 8192, "kv_cache_mode": "aggressive_prune" }
```
I'll report back metrics in 10m.

jin-ml: Also, fragmentation is a big factor — large entries produce slab blowouts and prevent reclaim. We should schedule slab compaction on nodes hosting their shards. That can be a short CPU spike but should free several GB. Can we do rolling compaction?

elaine-sre: I'll schedule rolling slab compaction on the 3 nodes during the quiet window (03:30 UTC). Also increasing eviction priority for >64k keys to cold_eviction now.

mike-eng-runtime: Longer term fixes: (a) enable per-tenant slab isolation so a noisy tenant can't steal the pool; (b) add a hard cap on large-key sizes in kvcache and reject overly large single entries; (c) improve autoscaler fallback to use warm spare capacity even if reserved_burst is low. I'll open a runtime ticket.

billing-jen: Noted the billing overage alert — I recommend a goodwill credit while we stabilize. I'll draft an approval request; please include estimated overage amount from the usage logs.

sam-solutions: FYI I already gave Skyline a quick playbook: if we enforce 8k and they still need more, propose a temporary Dedicated scale-up purchase or move their heaviest routes to a hot-shard with isolation. They're OK with credits if we buy them time.

mike-eng-runtime: Repro plan for eng: replay one of their 25k-token sessions in staging, observe KV growth and eviction churn, then iterate on compaction and eviction heuristics. Also test our denied-autoscale scenario.

sara-support: Early results: 10m after applying max_sequence_tokens=8192 the 429 rate dropped from ~18% -> ~2%, tail P99 latency improved ~45%. Customer still sees a handful of timeouts but overall better. They're holding off on escalation for now.

elaine-sre: Will follow up after compaction and dd the heap/slab hist after the rolling compaction. If fragmentation drops we can re-evaluate removing the temporary limit.

mike-eng-runtime: Thanks everyone. Action items assigned: 
- elaine-sre: run rolling compaction + post metrics (03:30 UTC)
- jin-ml: repro in staging + kvcache PR to add large-key cap
- billing-jen: credit request
- sam-solutions/sara-support: monitor customer and confirm stabilization

sara-support: closing loop — Skyline PM says the temporary limit is acceptable and appreciates the quick response. Will re-open if we see regression. :white_check_mark:
